skill.name: food-restaurants-email-marketing-specialist
skill.description: Plan restaurant and food-business email campaigns, diner-interest capture, reservation or order follow-up and audience segmentation. Use for menus, local offers, dining events and loyalty marketing; preserve booking, ordering and food-safety authority.
skill.summary: Draft restaurant email campaigns and customer journeys with consent safeguards, verified offers, and clear launch requirements.
skill.author: email-marketing-skills-hub

finding_verdicts.reason: The passage asks users to verify product documentation and account controls before specifying platform steps. It permits alternative platforms and requests no host inspection or reconnaissance.
The passage preserves marketing consent, suppression, and unsubscribe status. It contains no configuration library use, environment variable access, or credential retrieval.
The passage discusses optional marketing forms and minimizing collected customer information. It excludes sensitive dietary details from general popups and contains no system discovery instructions.
The booking and ordering system is named as the authority for business events, not a reconnaissance target. The passage prohibits promotional reminders from modifying bookings.
These are campaign quality checks for service coverage, cancellations, and offer validity, not infrastructure probing. The passage also prohibits sensitive tracking data and unauthorized paid orders.

content.value_statement: Restaurant promotions can fail when offers, customer permissions, and booking details are unclear. This skill guides campaign drafts, audience rules, and follow-up journeys with explicit launch checks.
actual_capabilities: Draft menu announcements, dining-event invitations, local promotions, and loyalty emails with subject lines, preheaders, body copy, and a primary call to action.
Define audience segments using location, permitted preferences, verified visit or order recency, and service mode.
Specify automated journeys with entry events, eligibility rules, delays, branches, exits, re-entry, overlap controls, and retry safeguards.
Review consent, suppression, offer terms, food-safety claims, and service constraints before launch.
Plan location-specific signup forms and capture-to-email mapping without assuming native platform integrations.
Define measurement using completed reservations, attended covers, fulfilled orders, repeat visits, and appropriate attribution limits.
limitations: Provides written guidance rather than a bundled sending service or executable platform integration.
Cannot establish live menu availability, prices, customer permissions, or booking status without current authoritative information.
Does not establish legal compliance, food safety, allergen guarantees, or alcohol promotion eligibility.
Does not guarantee campaign results or authorize sending, scheduling, data uploads, or account changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Local Menu Announcement
use_cases.description: Draft an email for a verified menu update with location details, current terms, and one ordering or reservation destination.

use_cases.title: Design Multi-Location Audience Rules
use_cases.description: Separate location preferences and consent scopes while preventing duplicate promotions and excluding suppressed contacts.

use_cases.title: Review a Post-Order Journey
use_cases.description: Specify feedback and repeat-visit branches using reliable order completion, cancellation, complaint, and recent-purchase data.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Menu Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a menu announcement for [restaurant] at [location]. Use [approved menu details] and [destination URL]. Include subject, preheader, body, and one CTA. Mark unknown terms.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Prepare a single campaign draft.

prompt_templates.title: Define an Eligible Audience
prompt_templates.prompt: Define audience rules for [offer] across [locations]. Use [available fields] and [consent rules]. Address preferences, suppressions, duplicates, and third-party customer permissions. List missing facts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Plan segmentation before selecting recipients.

prompt_templates.title: Specify a Follow-Up Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a post-order journey using [platform] and [authoritative events]. Specify eligibility, delays, timezone, branches, exits, re-entry, overlap, and retries. Handle complaints and recent purchases. Do not execute.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Design automation without changing live systems.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Campaign Launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [campaign draft], [audience rules], [offer terms], and [event mapping]. Identify consent, food-safety, service, attribution, and retry risks. Separate launch blockers from assumptions. Recommend authorized next steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review a campaign and its operational dependencies.

output_examples.input: Draft a Friday menu announcement for Harbor Kitchen. Friday dinner runs from 5 to 9 p.m. The booking URL is not supplied.
output: Subject: Friday dinner at Harbor Kitchen
Preheader: Plan your visit between 5 and 9 p.m.
Body: Join us for Friday dinner at Harbor Kitchen. View [approved menu] and reserve through [verified booking URL].
Launch checks: Confirm the location, date, timezone, booking destination, and audience permission before sending.

output_examples.input: Review a half-price delivery promotion claiming guaranteed nut-free meals. Service area, fees, kitchen controls, and third-party customer permissions are unverified.
output: Launch blockers: Remove the unsupported allergen guarantee. Confirm delivery coverage, fees, promotion timing, exclusions, and applicable customer permissions.
Audience rule: Hold contacts whose promotional permission is missing or unclear.
Draft direction: Use verified offer details and approved food-safety wording, with placeholders for unresolved terms.
Next action: Obtain approved operational facts and permission evidence. Do not send or upload customer data.

best_practices: Provide approved menu details, service areas, hours, timezone, offer terms, and authoritative booking or ordering sources before drafting.
Recheck consent and suppression immediately before sending, including delayed journeys and third-party customer lists.
Test cancellations, sold-out items, service complaints, duplicate events, and uncertain delivery outcomes before requesting launch authorization.
anti_patterns: Treating a signup, menu click, or marketplace purchase as permission for every promotion or brand.
Promising allergen safety, certification, availability, or profitability without verified operational evidence.
Sending campaigns, modifying bookings, or retrying uncertain sends merely because a draft or plan was requested.

faq.question: Does this skill send emails?
faq.answer: No bundled sending service is included. Live sending, scheduling, uploads, and account changes require suitable tools and applicable authorization.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is Poptin required?
faq.answer: No. Poptin is optional when it addresses a verified capture need. Existing email, reservation, ordering, and POS systems can remain in place.

faq.question: Can third-party delivery customers receive promotions?
faq.answer: Only when the channel establishes the required promotional permissions. Interest or purchase history alone does not establish marketing eligibility.

faq.question: Can the skill approve allergen-free claims?
faq.answer: No. Such claims require an approved operational basis and qualified food-safety oversight. Unverified claims should not appear in campaign copy.

faq.question: What happens when campaign details are missing?
faq.answer: The skill uses placeholders, separates verified facts from assumptions, and identifies launch blockers. It does not invent access, permissions, or results.
